mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Korean post-registration corporate registration extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Supreme Court Registration Office through the competent district court registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issue the certified original from the court registry; notarize the registrar signature before a Korean notary public; then obtain a Hague Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs if the destination state is an Apostille Convention member. For a non-member destination, after notarization obtain Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication and then consular legalization at the destination state embassy in Seoul. The apostille and consular legalization routes are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the ultimate corporate shareholder or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the ultimate beneficial owner or parent entity country of domicile, or Korean Supreme Court Registration Office if the parent is Korean
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain the original from the competent registry; notarize the registry official signature; if the issuing state is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, obtain an apostille from that state designated competent authority; if the issuing state is not an Apostille member, obtain official authentication from that state ministry of foreign affairs and then legalization from the Korean embassy or consulate in that state. Apostille and consular legalization remain alternative and mutually exclusive and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing formation and Korean counsel engagement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the corporate ultimate beneficial owner, notarized by a notary public in the notary jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the execution signatures before a notary in the state of execution; for an Apostille Convention state, have the designated competent authority issue an apostille; for a non-Apostille state, have the home state ministry of foreign affairs authenticate the document and then submit it to the Korean consular post in that state for legalization. These are mutually exclusive paths; do not add a Korean apostille to a document already consularized.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the proposed Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders through a Korean notary public before corporate registration, with final certificate after registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute the articles in Korean before a Korean notary public; then obtain a Hague Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for use in an Apostille Convention destination; for a non-Apostille destination, obtain Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication and then consular legalization from the destination state embassy in Seoul. The two authentication mechanisms are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be applied to the same document sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the ultimate beneficial owner primary banking relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Primary issuing bank of each ultimate beneficial owner or corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issue the letter on original bank letterhead and have the signing bank officer signature acknowledged before a notary; if the bank country is an Apostille Convention state, obtain an apostille from that country designated competent authority; if the bank country is not an Apostille state, obtain notarization, then home state ministry of foreign affairs authentication, and then legalization from the Korean consular post in that country. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and never sequential.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Each UBO, director, and authorized signatory must undergo enhanced due diligence against (i) the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit suspicious transaction reporting obligations under the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the US OFAC SDN List and CAPTA list; (iv) HM Treasury and EU consolidated lists; and (v) the Korean domestic list published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Financial Services Commission under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Screening must be continuous, risk-based, and include any politically exposed person (PEP) as defined by FATF Recommendations 12 and 22. A positive match requires immediate filing of a suspicious transaction report with the KoFIU, asset freeze assessment, and refusal or termination of the relationship unless a written license is obtained.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Service of the Supreme Court of Korea (Court Registry Information System)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be registered in Korean Hangul and no Chinese character or non-Korean script may serve as the primary legal trade name; foreign words may be transliterated only under the Korean Loanword Orthography rules, and an English alias is a secondary convenience that does not replace the Hangul name. The name clearance doctrine applies a four-tier convention: first tier is the distinctive element, second tier is the business-descriptive element, third tier is the legal form suffix Chusik Hoesa, and fourth tier is any separately registered foreign-language alias; the combination must not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered trade name in the same geographic registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for 30 days and may be renewed only by filing a fresh reservation request before the original expires; no automatic extension exists. If the registry rejects the name, the filer may file a written objection with the competent district court registry within seven days of receiving the rejection notice, identifying the legal basis for registrability and rebutting the examiner findings. For refusal based on a conflicting registered trade name, the filer may either submit written consent from the conflicting company or apply for cancellation of the conflicting mark. For refusal based on a prohibited financial term, the filer must first obtain written preliminary approval from the Financial Services Commission and then resubmit under the same receipt number. If the registry maintains the rejection, the filer may appeal to the Supreme Court under the Commercial Act registry procedure within fourteen days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a licensed discretionary multi-family office, a virtual office, shared co-working address, or commercial mailbox is rejected by the Financial Services Commission, the Financial Supervisory Service, the National Tax Service, and licensed custodian banks. Under Article 19 of the Commercial Act and Article 12(2) of the Framework Act on National Taxes, the registered office must be the actual place where corporate management is exercised, personnel are employed, compliance records are maintained, and client files are stored. A serviced office may be acceptable only if it is a dedicated leased unit with full-time staff and physical management autonomy, but a mere postal address is never sufficient because the National Tax Service will reclassify the corporate seat for local tax purposes and banks will refuse to open custody and interbank accounts.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 57 percent probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months by the National Tax Service, municipal district tax office, Financial Supervisory Service, or registry authorities because a multi-family office with custody wire and Swift interbank payment rails is classified as high-risk for AML. Inspection-trigger checklist: (1) missing lease certificate or sublease consent; (2) absence of a named resident compliance officer at the office; (3) no UBO interview availability at the registered address; (4) discrepancies between custody wire instructions and office location; (5) incomplete original AML and customer identification files; (6) reliance on part-time staff only; (7) offsite server without chain of custody; (8) board minutes not maintained at the registered office; (9) refusal to allow Financial Intelligence Unit inspection; and (10) signs that the address is only a virtual mailbox.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 288 to 317 and Article 393, including Article 289 on articles of incorporation, Article 295 on payment for subscribed shares, and Article 317 on registration of incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Section of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office, operating under the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office electronic commercial registration system
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation and the Standard Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: There is no statutory minimum paid-in capital under the Korean Commercial Act for a Chusik Hoesa. The promoters may fix the initial capital in the articles of incorporation, but the full subscription amount for the shares issued at incorporation must be paid in cash and deposited in a Korean bank before the registration application is filed. The bank issues a Capital Deposit Certificate evidencing the payment; the amount is not a blocked escrow in the ordinary sense, but it must remain on deposit and cannot be withdrawn for any purpose other than corporate expenses after registration is completed. If the company applies for a financial investment business license or registration under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, the Financial Services Commission will require minimum equity capital applicable to the license category, such as discretionary investment management or investment advisory, and a bank verification of paid-in capital must accompany the license dossier.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION NO. 2024-001 OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY] CO., LTD.

At a duly convened meeting of the Board of Directors of [Company] Co., Ltd. (the 'Company'), held at the registered office at [●], Seoul, Republic of Korea, at [●] o'clock KST on [●], 20[●], the following directors, constituting a majority of the entire Board and a quorum, were present: [Director A], [Director B], and [Director C]. The Chairman confirmed that notice of the meeting was given in accordance with the Korean Commercial Act and the Articles of Incorporation.

WHEREAS, the Company was incorporated as a Chusik Hoesa (Stock Corporation) under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea with the object of carrying on multi-family office and discretionary portfolio advisory services; and

WHEREAS, the founding shareholders have subscribed for the initial issued shares of the Company, and the full subscription amount of KRW [●] (the 'Paid-In Capital') has been deposited in [●] Bank, as evidenced by the Capital Deposit Certificate; and

WHEREAS, the Board is empowered pursuant to Article 393 of the Korean Commercial Act to make decisions on management and to appoint the Company's statutory officers; and

WHEREAS, the Company needs to designate its registered office, authorize banking arrangements for corporate funds and client money segregation, and appoint responsible officers before commencing operations.

NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. Subscription and Allotment of Shares. The subscription and allotment set out in the Subscription Schedule are hereby ratified and confirmed. The Paid-In Capital of KRW [●] is declared to be the initial paid-in capital of the Company, and the Capital Deposit Certificate shall be maintained in the Company's corporate records.

2. Banking Authorization. The Representative Director, Chief Financial Officer, and Compliance Officer are jointly and severally authorized to open and operate the Company's primary corporate bank accounts at [●] Bank, to sign mandates, to issue checks and transfer instructions as authorized by separate Board resolution, and to establish segregated client money accounts in order to preserve client assets separate from the Company's assets.

3. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office shall be and is hereby fixed at [●], [●]-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea. The Representative Director is authorized to execute and deliver the lease agreement, to receive service of process and official notices, and to file any address changes at the competent Registry and the Tax Office.

4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The following officers are appointed effective immediately: [●] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [●] as Chief Financial Officer; [●] as Compliance and Anti-Money Laundering Officer; and [●] as Corporate Secretary. Each officer shall exercise the powers specified by law, the Articles of Incorporation, and this resolution.

5. Regulatory Filing Authorization. The Representative Director and Compliance Officer are authorized to submit all applications and documents required for the financial investment business registration and related industrial licensing, and to execute such declarations, undertakings, and powers of attorney as the Financial Services Commission and the Financial Supervisory Service may require.

6. Ratification. All acts previously performed by the promoters and officers to establish the Company and open subscription accounts are hereby ratified, approved, and adopted as acts of the Company.

This resolution is effective as of the date set out above and shall remain in full force and effect until revoked by the Board or otherwise required by law.

CERTIFIED by the Corporate Secretary as a true and correct record of the proceedings of the First Board of Directors Meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (Commercial Registration System) and a Korean Notary Public authorized under the Notary Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters must first verify the availability of the proposed Korean corporate name through the Internet Registration Office. Once cleared, the promoters cause the Articles of Incorporation to be drafted in Korean, including the corporate name, business purpose expressly covering discretionary portfolio advisory for multiple family clients, initial capital, number of authorized shares, registered office, and director provisions, and then appear before a notary public for authentication. The notary verifies the identity of all promoters, confirms that the articles are not contrary to the Commercial Act or public policy, and records the certificate of authentication on the articles. After notarization, the article form becomes binding on the company and must not be altered except by a notarized amendment.
required_dossiers: Passports or resident registration cards of promoters
Name reservation certificate
Korean-language draft Articles of Incorporation
Business plan describing multi-family office services
Certificates of no disqualification for directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is refused for conflict, the promoter must immediately reserve a new name with the same authority. If the notary queries any clause, the promoter should submit an explanatory board memorandum or amend the offending provision, then re-attend the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Paid-In Capital Deposit and Issuance of Capital Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean commercial bank or securities company authorized to receive incorporation deposits
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, the promoters open a temporary share subscription account under the proposed corporate name and deposit the aggregate subscription amounts from each subscriber by bank remittance. The bank must issue a Capital Deposit Certificate addressed to the promoters stating the amount deposited, the account number, and the name of the depositor. The certificate is required for the court registration application. The capital must remain in the account and not be moved or withdrawn until registration is completed, except for the payment of registration fees after the application is accepted. The deposit certificate should be obtained in original form and kept with the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Subscriber identification
Share subscription list with individual amounts
Bank remittance receipts from each subscriber
Capital deposit certification form of the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines to issue the certificate or identifies a mismatch in subscriber details, correct the remittance records and request a restated certificate. Where a bank error causes rejection, select another bank, return the funds, and reopen the account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Section of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office, via the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two weeks after payment of capital, the promoters must file the incorporation registration application with the competent court registry, either electronically through the Internet Registration Office or in person. The filing must be accompanied by the notarized articles, original capital deposit certificate, a written statement confirming directors' acceptance, the first board resolution appointing the representative director, and proof of payment of registration and local education taxes. The registry will review compliance with the Commercial Act and issue a certificate of incorporation and seal certificate. Only after registration does the company legally acquire its separate corporate personality and capacity to open permanent bank accounts or execute binding contracts.
required_dossiers: Application for Commercial Registration (standard form)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital Deposit Certificate (original)
Consent to appointment signed by each director
First Board Resolution appointing representative director
Power of attorney if using agent
Registration tax payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court suspends or returns the application, the applicant must review the deficiency notice and submit the missing documents within the court's correction window. If the error concerns capital payment or articles, the promoters may need to amend and re-notarize the articles before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Business Registration and Corporate Identifier Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service local district office via HomeTax electronic filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days after registration, the representative director must file for business registration at the district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office. The local tax office will issue a Business Registration Certificate containing the corporate registration number under the Framework Act on National Taxes. The company must also apply for electronic tax invoice issuance, withhold income tax on employees, and register the corporate bank account with the tax authority. The business registration is essential for issuing tax invoices, claiming input VAT, and conducting regulated activities.
required_dossiers: Incorporation certificate (certificate of registered matters)
Seal certificate
Lease agreement or proof of occupied office
Representative director's identification and power of attorney
Business registration application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests proof of actual office use or landlord identification, provide the lease agreement and landlord's consent. In case of late filing, file promptly with the applicable lateness penalty or request a mitigation of sanction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Financial Investment Business License or Registration and AML/FIU Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Services Commission, Financial Supervisory Service, and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit under the Financial Services Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing discretionary portfolio advisory business for multiple families, the company must file an application for financial investment business license or registration under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, including the precise business scope of investment advisory and discretionary investment management. The application must demonstrate equity capital, organizational fitness, compliance and risk management policies, outsourcing arrangements, and investor protection plans. Concurrently, the company must submit a suspicious transaction reporting registration to the FIU and implement a customer due diligence program and a money laundering risk assessment. The regulator will conduct a solvency check and review the directors' and officers' eligibility, and issuance of the license is a condition precedent to business operations.
required_dossiers: FSCMA financial investment business application form
Certificate of incorporation and tax registration
Financial statements or capital verification certificate
Board resolution approving compliance program and AML policy
AML manual and customer due diligence templates
Statements of disqualification or eligibility for officers
Organizational chart and business plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSC requests supplementation, the company must file supplementary materials within the stated period. If licensing is denied, review the grounds, correct deficiencies, and re-apply or appeal through an administrative reconsideration before the FSC within the statutory deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to physical industry; the competent financial regulator is the Financial Services Commission, the Financial Supervisory Service, and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit for the multi-family office license and anti-money laundering registration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Financial Investment Business License/Registration under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act (Investment Advisory Services and Discretionary Investment Management) and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit Suspicious Transaction Reporting Registration

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea and Seoul Metropolitan Government environmental bureau for any office occupancy or interior fit-out matters
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable / Exempt - the activity is a non-industrial financial services office; no full EIA or environmental registration is required solely for the business. A simplified environmental notice may apply only to interior fit-out or premises renovation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or process effluent is generated. Domestic sewage and sanitary drainage are discharged to the municipal sewer system in accordance with the Water Environment Conservation Act, with no limit on the ordinary office load. Volatile organic compounds are not emitted in manufacturing quantities; office ventilation must comply with the Indoor Air Quality Control Act when the floor area exceeds the statutory threshold. Any hazardous waste such as spent toner, batteries, and electronic equipment must be transferred to a licensed recycling company under the Waste Control Act, and the manifest must be retained for five years.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before commencing operations, the registered office must obtain a certification of fire prevention from the relevant fire station in the form of an automatic fire suppression system inspection and evacuation plan approval; the building must have a certificate of occupancy issued by the Gu district office. The employer must register with the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency for workplace safety compliance, conduct a risk assessment, appoint a safety and health manager, and maintain fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, exit signs, and an emergency evacuation route per the Fire Fighting Facilities Maintenance Act and the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online portal: HomeTax at hometax.go.kr; customs clearance portal: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS at unipass.customs.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Determine whether the foreign non-resident entity has a Korean domestic place of business (fixed place of business, branch, office, or dependent agent). 2. If a domestic place of business exists, file an Application for Business Registration with the competent District Tax Office within 20 days from commencement of business. 3. Submit the following: articles of incorporation or equivalent constitutional documents; certificate of corporate existence or foreign corporation registration certificate; board resolution appointing the Korean responsible person and signed power of attorney; proof of the domestic place of business (lease agreement or legal proof of address); the commercial registry certificate of incorporation for a newly established Chusik Hoesa; and, if foreign capital is invested, the Foreign Investment Report filed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. 4. NTS validates the filing and assigns the statutory 10-digit Business Registration Number, which serves as the Korean TIN and VAT ID. 5. If the foreign non-resident entity has no domestic place of business but is required to account for Korean VAT (for example a foreign e-commerce or digital-services supplier), it must apply directly to NTS for non-resident VAT registration and will be issued a dedicated VAT ID for returns and payments. 6. Once registered, all VAT returns, corporate tax filings, tax invoice reporting, and withholding filings must be transacted through HomeTax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None - Korea does not provide a check-the-box or pass-through election; a Chusik Hoesa is automatically an entity-level taxpayer under the Corporate Tax Act, and hybrid mismatch rules are mandatory, not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None - no turnover threshold triggers registration; any person making taxable supplies in Korea must register for VAT regardless of volume. The KRW 80,000,000 simplified-taxpayer threshold applies only to certain individual entrepreneurs and does not exempt a Chusik Hoesa from registration or ordinary invoice duties.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are required for suppliers meeting the statutory e-invoice threshold, generally prior-year taxable supplies of KRW 100,000,000 or more; such suppliers must issue and transmit all tax invoices, including zero-rated export invoices, to NTS through HomeTax in structured electronic form, generally by the day following issuance. Large taxpayers and certified e-invoice service providers connect through HomeTax EDI/API interfaces. There is no physical fiscal stamp or governmental pre-clearance approval; anti-fraud control is executed through NTS HomeTax issue-number reconciliation, mandatory cash receipt reporting, payment card sales data, and matching with Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export declarations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Korea qualify for 0% VAT when an export declaration is accepted by Korea Customs Service, the goods are carried out under international transport documents, and export proceeds are received in foreign currency. Services supplied to a non-resident or foreign corporation qualify for 0% VAT where the service is used or consumed outside Korea; for a Multi-Family Office, discretionary portfolio advisory and asset-administration services to foreign families or offshore funds may be zero-rated only if the recipient is non-resident, the benefit is enjoyed outside Korea, and the fee is collected from abroad. Services used in Korea or supplied to a Korean recipient are taxable at 10%, and financial service activities that are exempt under the Value-Added Tax Act (such as certain custodial or fund services) do not generate input-VAT credits.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Goods Declaration (export clearance/export permit) filed with Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading for ocean freight or Air Waybill for air freight evidencing international transit
Zero-rated VAT tax invoice issued and transmitted through HomeTax

Foreign Exchange Purchase Certificate issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank (or equivalent foreign-currency receipt certificate) proving actual collection and repatriation of the export price
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service jointly match export declarations, transport documents, tax invoices, and foreign-exchange receipts. A zero-rating claim without complete documentary proof or actual foreign remittance is recharacterized as a domestic taxable supply; NTS assesses 10% VAT plus penalty taxes under the Value-Added Tax Act (up to 40% of the unlawful refund or understated tax, plus late-payment interest) and retroactively claws back any erroneous export refund. Deliberately fabricated export documentation is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for tax evasion, with imprisonment up to five years, fines up to three times the tax evaded, and loss of Customs export privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central monetary authority, together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) exercising foreign exchange policy oversight and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) as the core regulatory statute; the Bank of Korea also administers the Foreign Exchange Information Network and delegates day-to-day approval authority to designated foreign exchange banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely liberalised current account regime, allowing unbounded conversion for trade and service transactions subject to documentary verification and post-trade reporting. The capital account, however, while broadly open, remains subject to mandatory advance reporting, registration requirements for foreign direct investment (FDI) under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA), and prudential limits on debt-related inbound flows. For a multi-family office (MFO) structured as a Chusik Hoesa, inbound equity injections must be declared to the MOEF via a designated foreign exchange bank to obtain a certificate of foreign investment registration, which then permits KRW conversion at market rates. Profit remittance and dividend repatriation to non-resident shareholders require withholding tax compliance and a foreign exchange bank's confirmation of the underlying audited financial statements; there is no surrender requirement but the resident entity must file monthly foreign exchange transaction reports if an enterprise is classified as a business entity under FETA. Discretionary portfolio services involving cross-border securities or derivatives trigger further licensing under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act (FSCMA) and may require the MFO to hold a financial investment business license from the Financial Services Commission, making full capital account convertibility conditional on both regulatory licensing and transactional reporting, rather than on any blanket currency control restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 16 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the accompanying Foreign Exchange Transaction Regulations, export proceeds must be collected within 90 days from the export date (extendable to 180 days for general merchandise or longer for high-value goods under prior bank approval). There is no mandatory conversion ratio to KRW; exporters may hold foreign currency receipts in domestic foreign currency accounts or convert them at market rates, but they must be received in a domestic designated foreign exchange bank account and reported to the Bank of Korea within 30 days of collection via the Foreign Exchange Information Network. Failure to collect within the statutory timeline requires an explanation and may result in administrative penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility: South Korea does not recognise offshore digital EMI (Electronic Money Institution) or virtual account providers as licensed foreign exchange banks under FETA. Only designated domestic financial institutions (banks and certain brokerage houses) are permitted to execute foreign exchange transactions, open foreign currency accounts, and process cross-border settlement on behalf of resident corporate entities. An overseas fintech EMI cannot service the MFO's KRW current account or execute SWIFT interbank transfers with a valid Korean purpose code, and using such a provider would violate foreign exchange reporting obligations, leading to registration cancellation, fines, and potential criminal liability for the directors. Therefore, the MFO must maintain all operational and cross-border accounts with a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank, using fintech solutions only for ancillary payroll or reconciliation dashboards that integrate via open banking APIs without touching actual FX clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Chusik Hoesa with a high-risk MFO business scope, statutory directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) holding 20% or more of equity must physically appear at the designated foreign exchange bank's domestic branch for in-branch identity verification and a recorded compliance interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for foreign residents; non-resident directors may use a notarised power of attorney only after completing a video call with the bank's compliance officer and submitting apostilled identification, with the final board resolution and company seal registration (or equivalent statutory documentation under the Korean Commercial Act) executed locally. The bank will require additional face-to-face sessions for any discretionary investment mandate authorisation, and the MFO's licensed investment compliance officer (if any) must be present to clarify the source of funds and intended client profiles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained concentration of inbound funds from multiple family trusts without a transparent ownership chain, triggering a high-risk customer classification under the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendation 10 and Korea's Specified Financial Transaction Information Act.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (1) a group holding structure chart displaying all intermediate SPVs, trusts, and foundation layers; (2) genuine underlying trust deeds from jurisdictions of establishment with apostille or consular legalisation; (3) audited financial statements of each funding family for the last three years; (4) bank statements of the originating accounts for the previous six months; and (5) a written narrative explaining the economic rationale for pooling family wealth via a single Korean Chusik Hoesa.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discretionary portfolio advisory mandates involving investments in third-country marketable securities, which may trigger FSCMA investment licensing scrutiny and AML red flags for market manipulation or undisclosed beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit (1) a certified copy of the Financial Services Commission license or definitive legal exemption opinion from a qualified Korean law firm; (2) the complete investment policy statement and discretionary mandate agreement signed by each family client; (3) a list of portfolio managers and compliance officers with their FSC registration numbers; (4) a copy of the internal anti-money laundering manual and client due diligence procedures; and (5) regular transaction monitoring reports, including STR (suspicious transaction report) filing patterns for the historical period.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire activity into or out of countries on the FATF grey list or with high correspondent banking risk, causing the bank to request enhanced due diligence beyond standard KYC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (1) a detailed counterparty commercial explanation with underlying contracts or advisory service agreements; (2) sanctions screening results from a reputable database (e.g., OFAC, EU, UN) for every counterparty, transaction, and vessel/fund name; (3) for each high-risk transfer, the purpose code and supporting documentation (portfolio allocation reports, trade confirmations, execution broker statements); (4) a sworn declaration from the MFO's compliance officer confirming no shell activity; and (5) a commitment letter to provide post-transaction audit trails within 24 hours.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: KYC profile mismatch where the MFO's stated purpose is 'discretionary portfolio advisory' but the entity lacks a clear regulatory licence, suggesting possible unlicensed asset management or deposit-taking.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Append (1) the MFO's articles of incorporation and business registration certificate; (2) a legal opinion from a Korean securities law specialist confirming that the planned activities fall within the 'non-discretionary advisory' exemption or that the requisite FSCMA license application has been filed; (3) the bank's internal classification of the client as 'High-Risk Special License' and the MFO's acceptance of enhanced monitoring; (4) a copy of the client on-boarding file containing each family member's passport/UBO declaration, confirmed with the registry of family office beneficiaries; and (5) a signed declaration that the entity will not accept third-party client funds unless and until a full financial investment business licence is obtained.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity capital for the Korean Chusik Hoesa must be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the beneficial owner's corporate account to the MFO's designated foreign exchange bank (e.g., Hana Bank or Shinhan Bank) with the remittance purpose code AF-01 (foreign direct investment) under FIPA. The bank will issue a certificate of foreign investment registration after receiving the MT103, the NFC (Non-Resident Company) resolution approving the investment, and the passport/business registration of the investor. Funds must be denominated either in KRW or freely convertible currencies; if in USD, conversion to KRW occurs at the spot rate offered by the receiving bank upon execution of the foreign exchange sale contract (purchase/sale confirmation). For regulatory capital verification, the MFO must file a capital verification application with the Korean certified public accountant, attaching the certificate, the bank's currency receipt confirmation, and the board resolution, and then submit audited financial statements to the National Tax Service. Any delay beyond 90 days from the foreign investment declaration date requires re-declaration to the MOEF. Subsequent shareholder loans must be reported as offshore borrowing on the Foreign Exchange Information Network, and must comply with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act ceiling on debt-to-equity ratios for tax-assured interest deductions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade-related and service fee disbursements from the MFO's KRW account are processed through domestic clearing house (KFTC) KRW transfers for local expenses, while outbound foreign currency payments use SWIFT MT103 messages through the corporate internet banking channel. For portfolio management fees paid to overseas investment advisors or custodians, the MFO must prepare a fee invoice, a settlement instruction, and a signed service agreement, and the bank will verify the transaction purpose code (e.g., A0601 for consultancy service payments or A0901 for management fees) before releasing the USD or EUR wire. For intra-group loans or equity-like investments, the MFO may use Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) when financing trade with affiliated suppliers, or Documentary Collections (MT400/MT710) for invoice-backed settlements. The bank will require ex-post documentation under the Foreign Exchange Information Network for all outbound transfers exceeding USD 50,000, and the MFO must maintain original supporting vouchers for five years. For high-value securities purchases, the bank will require separate approval from the Bank of Korea if the aggregate cross-border outbound investment in foreign securities exceeds the annual foreign portfolio investment ceiling, and will enforce a T+2 settlement cycle using the SWIFT network and the execution broker's local custody clearing rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX contracts (Up to 1 year for trade/current account transactions and up to 5 years for capital account transactions) executed with the same designated foreign exchange bank, subject to prior underlying risk exposure documentation

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) transactions restricted to offshore entities or branches for speculative arbitrage; onshore MFO may enter NDFs only with bank permission for hedging of non-KRW currency exposures without physical delivery, provided the notional exposure is documented
Currency swaps permitted for real trade/investment hedging purposes with bank approval under FETA, limited to the maturity of the underlying asset or liability

Cross-currency interest rate swaps allowed for the MFO's external borrowings with the domestic bank acting as an intermediary, but require advance registration with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and a certificate of foreign capital admission

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Tax Return (Corporate Tax Base and Tax Payment) and audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax e-filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year entity: on or before March 31 immediately following the close of the fiscal year; for non-calendar-year entity: within 3 months from the fiscal year-end; one-month filing extension is available upon application to the NTS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory non-filing penalty of 20 percent of unpaid corporate income tax, 40 percent for fraudulent or dishonest non-filing, 10 percent underreporting penalty, 40 percent for unlawful underreporting, daily late-payment interest of approximately 0.025 percent per day, asset seizure, tax lien registration and criminal referral under the Framework Act on National Taxes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surcharge Return (Local Income Tax on corporate taxable income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax authority (Seoul Metropolitan Government or relevant provincial city) via WeTax local tax e-filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same statutory deadline as national corporate income tax: March 31 for calendar-year taxpayers or within 3 months after non-calendar year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surtax of 20 percent of unpaid local surtax, 40 percent in fraudulent cases, underreporting surtax of 10 percent to 40 percent, late-payment interest, business premises seizure and denial of local tax payment certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report Registration and Filing in the FSS External Audit Report System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via the external audit report registration system and DART electronic disclosure system; audited financial statements must accompany the NTS corporate tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the independent auditor issues the audit report and no later than the statutory annual financial statement approval cycle; for calendar-year licensed entities, the completed audit opinion must be available for the March 31 tax filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty up to KRW 50,000,000 for failure to register or late registration of the audit report; FSC corrective orders, disqualification of the auditor, and criminal sanctions for omission of material facts or knowingly false audit reports.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' General Meeting and Approval of Balance Sheet, Income Statement, Retained Earnings Appropriation and Statutory Auditor Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate organ; minutes maintained in the corporate minute book at the registered office; not registered with the court unless articles of incorporation are amended
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be convened within 3 months after the close of each fiscal year; for calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, on or before March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court fine up to KRW 5,000,000 against non-compliant officers under the Korean Commercial Act; failure to approve financial statements may cause rejection of corporate tax return and FSC action against the licensed multi-family office.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report and Internal Control Report for Licensed Multi-Family Office / Discretionary Portfolio Advisory Business
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the FSS electronic filing system for financial investment business entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the close of the business year; for December fiscal year-end, filing due by March 31, subject to FSC-granted extension in exceptional circumstances
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 50,000,000, restriction or revocation of the financial investment business license, corrective orders, and civil or criminal liability for false filing under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML/CFT Compliance Report, Beneficial Ownership Register Certification and Suspicious Transaction Reporting Self-Assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU), Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory Service under the Act on Prohibition of Money Laundering
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual internal-control and AML compliance certification must be completed and submitted no later than the annual business report deadline for the licensed multi-family office; suspicious transactions must be reported within 3 days of detection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines, imprisonment for willful AML failures, administrative fines up to KRW 30,000,000, license revocation, and personal liability of compliance officers for non-reporting or failure to update beneficial ownership files.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Notification / Change of Foreign Shareholder or Beneficial Owner Reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) one-stop foreign investment support center integration system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No separate annual filing is due when no shareholding change occurs; any acquisition or transfer causing a foreign investor to hold 10 percent or more of shares, or any subsequent change in the foreign-invested enterprise, must be reported within 30 days of the underlying event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty up to KRW 5,000,000 for failure to file; foreign-invested enterprise status, legal protections, tax incentives and dividend remittance privileges may be denied, clawed back, or suspended.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, an independent certified CPA audit is compulsory for: (i) all listed companies regardless of asset size; (ii) unlisted stock companies with total assets of KRW 12,000,000,000 or more, approximately USD 9,000,000, at the end of the fiscal year; (iii) unlisted companies with KRW 7,000,000,000 or more in total assets and a debt-to-equity ratio above the threshold prescribed by Presidential Decree; and (iv) all licensed financial investment business entities, including discretionary portfolio advisers and multi-family offices, irrespective of asset size, under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act and Financial Supervisory Commission regulations. For this high-risk licensed multi-family office, the FSC will require an independent statutory audit without regard to the general 12 billion KRW balance-sheet threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for listed companies, licensed financial entities and all companies required to present consolidated financial statements; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles for non-publicly accountable entities (K-GAAP / Korean SME Accounting Standards) is available only to smaller unlisted companies not subject to mandatory external audit; the licensed multi-family office must prepare annual financial statements under K-IFRS, with the independent auditor's opinion complying with the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and the Application Standards on Auditing.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not maintain a general public beneficial-ownership register for ordinary Chusik Hoesa corporations. However, for a licensed high-risk multi-family office, FSC AML/CFT rules and the Act on Prohibition of Money Laundering require the company to identify and verify all client and corporate beneficial owners, maintain a written beneficial-ownership and source-of-funds dossier, and certify the beneficial-ownership register annually in the AML internal-control compliance report submitted to KoFIU and FSS. Any share transfer resulting in a change of 10 percent or more of the share capital, or any change in control, must be recorded in the corporate shareholder register within 30 days; if a foreign investor notification threshold is crossed, the transfer must also be reported to MOTIE/KOTRA within the same 30-day window. The corporate secretary must perform an annual on-site statutory register audit, paginate and initial each register, verify that share transfer instruments are properly stamped, and produce a register audit certificate for the board of directors.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Shareholders) with transfer history and share-transfer consents
Register of Statutory Auditors / Audit Committee members
Register of Charges, Pledges or Security Interests over Korean movable assets and intangible rights
Minute Book of Shareholders' General Meetings
Minute Book of Board of Directors' Meetings
Foreign Investment and UBO CDD Record File

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $1,200 - $3,500 for licensed corporate secretarial agent service; $4,000 - $12,000 for a premium Seoul Gangnam registered office lease and receiving-agent infrastructure
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $8,000 - $25,000 for a typical multi-family office / discretionary portfolio advisory entity, depending on client fund flow, number of underlying portfolios, cross-border custody assets and audit complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: South Korea applies progressive corporate income tax rates: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% on income between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion; 24% on income above KRW 20 billion. Incentive regimes include: (i) Qualifying foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones may receive a 100% corporate income tax exemption for the first 5 years and a 50% reduction for the following 2 years; (ii) R&D tax credits under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act for qualifying R&D expenditures; (iii) facility investment credits and job creation credits; (iv) no patent box regime, but IP income is taxable as ordinary business income subject to ordinary tax rates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form (법인세 과세표준 및 세액신고서) filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax system (www.hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year. For a standard calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, the deadline is March 31 of the following year. An extension of up to 1 month may be granted for certain foreign-invested enterprises or when the return is prepared and submitted by a licensed tax accountant or CPA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification, fiscal year, and non-resident shareholder roster
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Chusik Hoesa controlled or owned by non-residents, attach Schedule 11 (Non-Resident Shareholders Roster) and disclose each non-resident shareholder's jurisdiction of tax residence, ownership percentage, and Tax Residency Certificate validity. This is required to determine bilateral tax treaty eligibility for outbound dividends and to prevent look-through or treaty-shopping abuses.

Report full worldwide gross revenue from discretionary portfolio advisory, custody, and SWIFT interbank services. A domestic Korean entity is taxed on worldwide income; therefore, no PE apportionment is allowed. Adjust intercompany income to arm's length under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, and ensure all cross-border wire transfers are traceable and economically substantiated.

Expense deductions for management fees, royalties, or interest paid to foreign affiliated parties are denied unless substantiated by valid contracts, actual service delivery, and arm's length pricing. For a multi-family office, administrative services performed outside Korea should be supported by technical fee data, cost allocation, and a service-level agreement. If the overseas service provider lacks economic substance, the full payment is disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable income, foreign-source income, and tax treaty adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korean domestic corporations cannot choose to exclude foreign-source income; instead, such income is fully taxable subject to a foreign tax credit. Qualifying dividends received from foreign subsidiaries may benefit from a participation exemption under Article 18-3 of the Corporate Tax Act if the Korean parent holds at least 10% of the foreign subsidiary's shares for a minimum of 1 year and the subsidiary is not a hybrid entity. For MFO clients, ensure proper documentation of underlying fund distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base and computed tax (각 사업연도 소득금액)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the progressive rates: 9% on the first KRW 200 million, 19% on the next bracket, and 24% on excess income. A multi-family office with typical Korean-tested net income will usually fall into the 19% bracket. Transfer pricing adjustments, if any, must be reflected before applying the rate schedule. Non-resident shareholders should note that corporate-level tax is computed before any dividend withholding obligation is triggered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and foreign tax credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include applicable tax credits: Research and Development credits under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, foreign tax credits under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, and credits for eligible venture investment or job creation. For non-resident financial institutions, no Korean tax credit is available for taxes paid abroad on cross-border custody fee income; instead, withholding tax may be reduced under a relevant treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax amount and local income tax surcharge reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Show the national corporate income tax liability. Separately compute the local income tax surcharge at 10% of the national corporate income tax. The aggregate tax burden is effectively 9% to 24% plus a 2.4% local surcharge on the taxable amount (i.e., 10% of the national tax). For purposes of the whitepaper, the effective headline rate including local surcharge is 26.4% in the top bracket.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax declaration for non-resident earnings
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: On the same annual return, the Korean entity, as a payer, must report withholding tax on dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-residents. The statutory aggregate withholding rate is 22% (20% national plus 2% local surcharge). If a tax treaty provides a reduced rate, attach the treaty relief application, TRC, and beneficial ownership declaration. Withholding must be remitted by the 10th of the month following the payment month.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the corporate income tax return triggers an additional income tax surcharge of 20% of the unpaid tax if the filing is made after a formal demand; otherwise, for a voluntary late filing, the surcharge is 10% of the under-reported tax. A negligence penalty of 10% applies for careless misstatement. Unpaid tax accrues daily overdue interest at approximately 0.022% per day (about 8.03% per annum). Deliberate omission or fraudulent returns fall under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, carrying imprisonment of up to 3 years or fines of up to three times the evaded tax. Where a corporation fails to withhold and remit non-resident withholding tax, a penalty of 100% of the unwithheld amount is imposable, and the directors may be personally liable for that penalty.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate (20% national dividend withholding tax plus 10% local income tax surcharge on that tax, yielding an additional 2%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding under a South Korea income tax treaty, the non-resident payee must: (1) provide a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its home tax authority; (2) submit the Secretary of Tax Collection's Form No. 'Application for Tax Exemption/Reduction under Tax Treaty' to the withholding agent prior to payment; (3) file a beneficial ownership declaration confirming that the payee is the true owner of the income and has no contractual or legal obligation to pass the payment to another person; (4) if the payee is an intermediary or a conduit entity without real commercial substance, treaty relief must be refused. The withholding agent is required to attach the full treaty claim package to its corporate tax return and must remit any partially withheld amount to the National Tax Service. Korean tax law applies an anti-abuse rule whereby treaty benefits are denied for back-to-back financing or intra-company royalty arrangements that lack substance and business purpose.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For interest and royalties paid to non-residents, the statutory withholding rate is 22% aggregate (20% national plus 2% local surcharge). Under applicable Korean tax treaties, interest is commonly reduced to 10% or 15%, and royalties to 10% or 15%, provided the beneficial owner does not have a permanent establishment in Korea to which the income is attributable. For interest derived from bank loans or financing transactions sourced from a Korean company, treaty withholding may be eliminated if the DTA grants exclusive taxation to the residence country and the Korean source is not connected to a PE.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File (contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation) is required where the annual consolidated gross revenue of the Korean taxpayer equals or exceeds KRW 10 billion; Master File is required when such revenue reaches KRW 100 billion. For all intercompany cross-border transactions exceeding KRW 1 billion, a detailed functional and risk analysis, arm's length benchmark, and transfer pricing reports must be available upon request. The National Tax Service may impose documentation penalties up to 30% of the adjusted amount where required documentation is not maintained.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not have a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute analogous to Gulf states, but the equivalent doctrines are embedded in the Corporate Tax Act and the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs. The tax authority applies a substance-over-form test and may recharacterize transactions through the 'actual place of management' doctrine. For a multi-family office, the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) must be performed by employees and systems located in Korea: discretionary investment decisions, contractual due diligence, portfolio risk management, trade execution, and custody wire instruction approval. If these CIGA are in fact performed abroad and the Korean entity is merely a contracting shell, the Korean corporate veil may be pierced, and the entity may be denied treaty benefits on its own outbound payments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Profit Stripping and Tax Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive management fees, royalties, or interest to a non-resident parent, sister entity, or beneficiary without actual services, without arm's length benchmarking, and with no economic substance in the offshore payee; artificially shifting the multi-family office's discretionary management fees and custody revenue into a zero or low tax state.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service will re-determine income upward under Article 5 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs and impose an under-reporting surcharge of 10% of the adjusted tax, plus daily overdue interest at 0.022% per day. If documentation is missing, an additional penalty up to 30% of the adjusted amount may apply. If the adjustment exceeds a material threshold and is willful, the matter is referred for criminal charging under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act with fines of up to three times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorized the false transfer prices are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax and penalties; the National Tax Service can attach personal bank accounts, real estate, and receivables. Civil restitution orders may pierce the corporate veil, and travel bans (blacklisting as delinquent taxpayers) are automatically imposed for unpaid arrears exceeding a statutory threshold. Criminal conviction carries imprisonment of up to 3 years; if the evaded tax exceeds KRW 500 million, the recommended minimum imprisonment rises to 2 years and may reach 5 years for organized fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Asset Management, AML, and Custody Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a multi-family office that provides discretionary portfolio advisory and executes high-value custody wires and SWIFT interbank payments without a license under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act (FSCMA), and simultaneously failing to file suspicious transaction reports, KYC documentation, and customer due diligence records required by the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 447 of the FSCMA, an unregistered financial investment business is punishable by imprisonment of not more than 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 200 million, or both. For aggravating circumstances involving systemic AML failures, the enforcement authorities may also impose administrative fines under the Financial Transactions Reports Act and orders to terminate business. The Financial Supervisory Service may refer the case to the prosecution with recommendation for criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable for the illegal profits derived from unlicensed asset management and for any client losses caused by unlawful execution. The corporate veil is pierced to attach personal assets of the directors, and they can be included in the public National Tax Delinquent List, triggering severe travel restrictions and reputational damage. Criminal convictions under the FSCMA carry actual imprisonment of up to 5 years, with foreign directors subject to exit bans pending trial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Treaty Shopping and Economic Substance Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a Korean Chusik Hoesa solely to invoice management fees, receive dividends or interest from Korean client assets, and then distribute funds to a foreign principal or beneficiary while all CIGA are performed offshore; using a conduit entity in a favourable DTA jurisdiction to obtain a 5% or 10% dividend withholding rate on outbound profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 2-3 of the Corporate Tax Act allows the tax authority to disregard a corporate entity that is not established for real business purposes, and Korean tax treaties contain, or incorporate through OECD rules, a limitation-on-benefits or principal purpose test. A sham entity is taxed as a transparent vehicle, and all treaty relief is denied. In addition, a penalty of 50% of the under-withheld tax is imposed for intentional misuse of a treaty exemption or reduction. The National Tax Service may impose a special audit and criminal penalty under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act for the intentional concealment of beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly operate a sham service company will face civil liability under Article 401 of the Commercial Act for causing tax losses, including restitution of treasury funds. Tax arrears and penalties are personally collectible when the entity lacks substantial business activity; travel bans are automatic for delinquent combined taxes exceeding KRW 100 million. If treaty-shopping is proven, directors may be prosecuted for fraud under the Tax Evasion Punishment Act and sentenced to up to 5 years in prison, with foreign directors banned from re-entry into Korea after release.
